statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low, with index futures halted across the entire forecast window.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold for all 24 forecast hours because every one of them falls inside the CME weekend halt, which leaves no tradeable path through which mean reversion could fail. The last observed structure was Friday's completed retracement into the close, not repeated extension after failed pullbacks. The elevated Stress reading describes a steep long end, Brent above 100 dollars and a disrupted Strait of Hormuz rather than an observed one-way Nasdaq-100 path, and the G7 reserve release eases that energy channel. The first opportunity for fresh price-path evidence is the Sunday futures restart at 22:00Z, which lies beyond this window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 weekend halt: Tail low after Friday's record probe was fully retraced; G7 reserve release eases the energy channel while a steep long end keeps Stress elevated
body: Friday closed the Nasdaq-100 at 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% and a record close, after probing an intraday record of 31,017.53 and then giving back roughly 210 points to finish near the session low of 30,737.07. That completed retracement is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure this framework treats as Tail evidence, and it is the last observable price path before CME equity-index futures halted at 21:00Z. Every hour of the published forecast window falls inside that halt, which does not end until the Sunday restart at 22:00Z, beyond this horizon. The session was driven by a soft September employment report: 29,000 jobs added against roughly 90,000 expected, unemployment up to 4.2% from 4.1% and average hourly earnings at 0.1% month over month. Bond traders cut October rate-hike odds to about 16% from roughly 64% a week earlier, and technology led with Nvidia touching intraday records. Volatility priced the move calmly, with VIX settling at 15.31, down 6.59%, at the low end of a 15.30-16.24 range rather than bid into the weekend. Stress stays in the elevated band on the rate and energy backdrop rather than on index structure. The long end remains steep, with the 10-year near 5.28% and the 30-year near 5.63% at Friday's close against the latest H.15 publication of 4.78% at two years and 5.24% at ten. Brent is last marked near 102.25 dollars and WTI near 91 dollars after touching a one-month low of 88.06 dollars intraday, and the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted after three tankers were struck by projectiles on 30 September. Offsetting that, the G7 agreed on 2 October to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel reserves over four months with a front-loaded tranche in the first 20 days, and Middle Eastern crude exports are reported close to pre-war levels. Confidence is high: verified index level and range, volatility, yields, oil and the forward calendar are all in hand, and the halt that dominates the forecast is certain rather than inferred. The shared Finviz context file was read and not used, because its latest collection is dated 29 September and reports partial status, which places it well outside the 90-minute freshness contract.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span the back half of Friday's payroll session and the first half-day of the weekend halt. Tail sat at 20 through the European morning, firmed to 24 into the 12:30Z payroll release and reached 25 and then 27 across the 13:30Z cash open as the index gapped up and extended toward its intraday record, which is the only stretch of the window that produced an orange state. Once the advance stalled and price retraced roughly 210 points into a close near the session low, Tail fell back to 22 and held between 21 and 23 through the U.S. afternoon. After the 21:00Z futures halt it decayed steadily through 14, 11 and 9 to 5 at the most recent assessment, with dominant mode moving from trend-up through mixed to normal. Stress fell more slowly, from 76 to 59, because the steep long end and the energy and Hormuz backdrop persisted after the session closed.
outlookSummary: All 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt: index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, which is beyond this horizon. With no tradeable session there is no mechanism for sustained mean-reversion failure, so Tail is projected to hold between 4 and 5 and every hour maps to EA_ON and green. Stress eases from 57 to 52 as the G7 reserve release and the recovery in Middle Eastern crude exports offset a steep long end and continued Hormuz disruption, remaining in the elevated band throughout. Confidence declines gently from 88 to 82 to reflect Friday's price evidence ageing rather than any conflict in it. No danger window is published, because an evidence-based window requires a tradeable session. The hours that would carry the weekday cash open, power hour and European pre-open are named as structural checkpoints only, and no reopen gap premium is applied to any hour, since the restart lies outside the window. The first scheduled catalyst after this horizon is ISM Services on Monday at 14:00Z, followed by FOMC minutes on Wednesday at 18:00Z.
